questions.q: The probability of men getting a certain disease is $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and that of women getting the same disease is $\dfrac{1}{5} .$ The blood test that identifies the disease gives the correct result with probability $\dfrac{4}{5}$. Suppose a person is chosen at random from a group of $30$ males and $20$ females, and the blood test of that person is found to be positive. What is the probability that the chosen person is a man?
questions.solution:
We have $30$ males and $20$ females.

$P\left(males\right) = \dfrac{30}{50} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

$P\left(females\right) = \dfrac{20}{50} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

Required probability $= \dfrac{\left(1\right) + \left(3\right)}{\left(1\right) + \left(3\right) + \left(5\right) + \left(7\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{5} + \dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{5}}{\dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{4}{5} + \dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{5} \times \dfrac{4}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{4}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{5}}$

$= \dfrac{1550}{\dfrac{15}{50} + \dfrac{16}{125}} = \dfrac{75}{107}$

questions.q: If a 3-digit number is randomly chosen, what is the probability that either the number itself or some permutation of the number (which is a 3 -digit number) is divisible by 4 and 5 ?
questions.solution:
We need 3 -digit number which is divisible by $4 \ \text{ and } 5$ both.
i.e. their last two digits are
$00,20,40,60 \ \text{ and } 80$
Now, ending with 00 are '9'.
$\{100,200, \ldots \ldots, 900\}$
If digit repeat other than ' 0 ' then they are
$\{220,440,660,880\}$
but 220 numbers can be permuted according to the condition as $\{220,202\}$
So, there are ' 8 ' other favorable cases.
If the number have no digit repeated like 320.
320 can be permuted in 4 ways.
$\{302,230,320,203\}$
So, such numbers are $8 \times 4 \times 4=128$
Total favorable $=9+8+128=145$
So, required prob. $=\frac{145}{900}=\frac{29}{180}$

questions.q: A box contains coupons labeled $1,2,3$....n. A coupon is picked at random and the number $\mathrm{x}$ is noted. The coupon is put back into the box and a new coupon is picked at random. The new number is $y$. Then the probability that one of the numbers $\mathrm{x}$, y divides the other is (in the options below [r] denotes the largest integer less than or equal to $\mathrm{r}$ )
questions.solution:
Let $x=1$
favourable out comes $(1,1),(1,2) \ldots \ldots(1, n)$ no. of favourable out comes when $x=1$
$$
=\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{1}\right]
$$
$\therefore$ no. of favourable out comes when $x=1$ or $y=1$
$$
=2\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{1}\right]-1
$$
no. of favourable out comes when $x=2$ or $y=2$ but $x \neq 1, y \neq 1$
$$
2\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{2}\right]-1
$$
Similarly
no. of favourable out comes when $x=k$ or $y=k$ but $x, y \notin\{1,2, \ldots . . k-1\}$
$$
2\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{k}}\right]-1
$$
So probability $=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left[\frac{n}{k}\right]-(1+1 \ldots . . n \text{ times })}{n^{2}}$
$$
=\frac{2}{\mathrm{n}^{2}} \sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{n}\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{k}}\right]-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}
$$

questions.q: A man tosses a coin 10 times, scoring 1 point for each head and 2 points for each tail. Let $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{K})$ be the probability of scoring at least $\mathrm{K}$ points. The largest value of $\mathrm{K}$ such that $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{K}) > 1 / 2$ is $-$

Ways to make the sum $K$ is coefficient of $x^{K} in \left(x+x^{2}\right)^{10}
Coefficient of $x^{K} in x^{10}(1+x)^{10}$
Coefficient of $x^{K-10} in (1+x)^{10}$
Which is ${ }^{10} $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{K}-$10}So ways to $make sum minimum \mathrm{K} is${ }^{10} $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{K}-$10}+{ }^{10} $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{K}-$9}+{ }^{10} $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{K}-$8}+\ldots . .+{ }^{10} $\mathrm{C}_{10}$
Probability
$\begin{aligned}

&=1-\frac{{ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_{0}+\ldots \ldots . .+{ }^{10} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{K}-11}}{2^{10}} \gt \frac{1}{2}

questions.q: Ravi and Rashmi are each holding $2$ red cards and $2$ black cards (all four red and all four black cards are identical). Ravi picks a card at random from Rashmi and then Rashmi picks a card to random from Ravi. This process is repeated a second time. Let $p$ be the probability that both have all $4$ cards of the same colour. Then, $p$ satisfies
questions.solution:
It is given that, Ravi and Rashmi are each holding $2$ red cards and $2$ black cards (all four red and all four black cards are identical).

Let Ravi picks a Red card from Rashmi and Rashmi picks black card from Ravi and in second time also Ravi picks a red card from Rashmi and Rashmi picks black card from Ravi, then finally Ravi have four red cards and Rashmi have four black cards, then probability of such event is

$\dfrac{C1 2}{C1 4} \times \dfrac{C1 2}{C1 5} \times \dfrac{C1 1}{C1 4} \times \dfrac{C1 1}{C1 5} = \dfrac{4}{400} = \dfrac{1}{100}$

Similarly, the probability if at the end Ravi have four black and Rashmi have four red cards is $\dfrac{1}{100}$.

So, required probability $= \dfrac{1}{50} = 2 % = p \le 5 %$
